minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard fire and police FY21 budget presentations; its only vote was a small training transfer.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee approved a small transfer from the advertising and dues lines to the meetings line to cover more members attending trainings.
The fire chief presented the FY21 budget, a paramedic plan and capital requests; an above-target call-back minimum request was not funded by the town manager.
The retiring police chief presented the department's FY21 budget and a ten-year plan; no vote was taken.
The town manager reported a lower new growth estimate because a solar project was delayed, and the revenue side has been adjusted.
The town manager also reported a favorable health insurance rate and a dispatch assessment voted below the estimate used.

why_it_matters: A lower new growth estimate means less added tax revenue for FY21, while the health insurance and dispatch savings ease some cost pressure on the town and school budgets.
The fire paramedic plan and the police ten-year plan point to service and staffing commitments that will come back as budget lines at Town Meeting.
watch_next: The assessing consultants' new growth presentation and the debt project are to be added to the committee's agenda for the following week.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the $60 and $20 transfer to the meetings line and on the $40,600 new growth and $15K dispatch figures. Ours lacks the roll call and most members, and the official minutes omit many figures we heard (health insurance, overlay, fire call). The dues line number differs (573000 vs 53700), and the police chief's name was misheard (Moreno vs Marino).
